problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\frac{{t}^{5}}{5},\,3{t}^{2}-1⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$

feedback.problem:
The position vector $r(t)$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2},\,2{t}^{4}-{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t.$

$a=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{4}-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{2}-8t,\,8{t}^{3}-2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-8t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8{t}^{3}-2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨6t-8,\,24{t}^{2}-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$
